cohort: The study included 100 OB-GYNs who gave birth between January 2012 and April 2022 and a matched control group of 200 non-medical background women.
finding: OB-GYN mothers did not significantly differ from non-physician women in Cesarean section rates and most pregnancy complication incidences, except for a lower incidence of postpartum hemorrhage (0% vs. 5.5%) among OB-GYNs.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were similar between OB-GYNs (32%) and non-physicians (36.5%).
